name: Non-specific Autoimmune Cerebellar Ataxia with Characteristic Antibodies
aliases: Paraneoplastic and Non-paraneoplastic Autoimmune Cerebellar Degeneration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Autoimmune Cerebellar Ataxia

criteria.description: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia with gait and limb incoordination
Detection of characteristic autoantibodies targeting cerebellar antigens (e.g., anti-Yo, anti-Hu, anti-Tr, anti-GAD)
Exclusion of alternative causes of cerebellar ataxia including genetic, metabolic, infectious, and toxic etiologies
Supportive cerebrospinal fluid findings such as mild lymphocytic pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands
Clinical improvement or stabilization with immunomodulatory treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with detection of characteristic autoantibodies and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often supported by CSF analysis and response to immunotherapy but these are not mandatory.

common.symptomName: Anti-regulator of G protein signaling 8 antibody positivity

laboratory: Presence of characteristic autoantibodies (anti-Yo, anti-Hu, anti-Tr, anti-GAD, others)
Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar atrophy or T2 hyperintensities in cerebellar cortex
FDG-PET may show hypometabolism in cerebellum
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; genetic causes excluded
other: Improvement or stabilization with immunotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis)

distinguishingFeatures: Progression over years without immunotherapy response
Oligoclonal bands but different clinical presentation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cerebellar symptoms over weeks to months
references: Graus F, et al. Autoimmune cerebellar ataxia: clinical and immunological features. Lancet Neurol. 2010.
Hadjivassiliou M, et al. Autoimmune cerebellar ataxia: clinical, immunological and therapeutic aspects. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2016.
Orphanet Report: Non-specific autoimmune cerebellar ataxia with characteristic antibodies (ORPHA:624259)
